research_page.title: Bapineuzumab in mild-to-moderate AD (Phase 3)
research_page.description: Two Phase 3 trials showed the anti-amyloid antibody bapineuzumab failed to improve clinical outcomes, despite engaging biomarkers in APOE4 carriers.
research_page.authors_line_md: Salloway et al. — Janssen Alzheimer Immunotherapy and Pfizer
research_page.takeaway_md: Bapineuzumab did not slow cognitive or functional decline in patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. While the drug proved it could engage its biological targets—stabilizing brain amyloid and lowering CSF phospho-tau in APOE4 carriers—these changes failed to produce clinical benefits. The drug's narrow therapeutic window, driven by dose-dependent amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA-E), ultimately led to the termination of the highest dose and the eventual abandonment of the program.
key_findings_md: Bapineuzumab failed to improve primary cognitive (ADAS-cog11) or functional (DAD) scores at 78 weeks in either APOE4 carriers or noncarriers (paper, Abstract).
The drug stabilized brain amyloid accumulation on PIB-PET and significantly reduced CSF phospho-tau in APOE4 carriers compared to placebo (paper, Key Biomarker Outcomes).
ARIA-E occurred in 15.3% of bapineuzumab-treated carriers, reaching 27.3% in APOE4 homozygotes, compared to 0.2% on placebo (paper, Safety).
Symptomatic ARIA-E rates forced the premature discontinuation of the highest evaluated dose (2.0 mg/kg) across the program (paper, Study Design and Treatment).
research_page.methods_md: Two parallel double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials enrolled 2,452 patients aged 50 to 88 with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease (MMSE 16-26). One trial enrolled 1,121 APOE4 carriers; the other enrolled 1,331 noncarriers. Participants received intravenous bapineuzumab or placebo every 13 weeks for 78 weeks ([NCT00575055](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00575055), [NCT00574132](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00574132)).
research_page.trial_evidence_md: These pivotal North American trials ([NCT00575055](/trials/bapineuzumab-nct00575055) and [NCT00574132](/trials/bapineuzumab-nct00574132)) conclusively demonstrated a lack of clinical efficacy for intravenous bapineuzumab. Consequently, sponsors terminated the entire clinical development program in August 2012, including parallel global trials ([NCT00676143](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00676143) and [NCT00667810](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00667810)).
research_page.sentiment_md: Public perception is largely negative, heavily shaped by the severe financial losses investors suffered when these high-profile trials failed to meet primary endpoints. Within the scientific community, sentiment is more nuanced; researchers view the confirmed biomarker modifications as a critical biological proof-of-concept for the [amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis), arguing it proves the target was engaged but suggests interventions must happen earlier in the disease course.
caveats_md: The premature discontinuation of the 2.0 mg/kg bapineuzumab dose severely limited the ability to evaluate whether higher-dose therapy could have driven clinical efficacy.
Biomarker substudies for PIB-PET and CSF analysis relied on very small sample sizes, limiting the statistical power of the biological findings, particularly among noncarriers.
relates_to_md: [Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — Bapineuzumab provided the first major Phase 3 evidence that clearing amyloid does not automatically rescue cognition in symptomatic patients.
[Biomarkers](/research/biomarkers) — The 36.1% amyloid-negative rate among noncarriers highlighted the absolute necessity of using PET or CSF screening to confirm diagnosis before trial enrollment.

[Aducanumab in early AD](/research/papers/aria-aducanumab-emerge-engage) — A subsequent anti-amyloid antibody that engaged the same biological targets but also grappled with dose-limiting ARIA safety challenges.

trial_pages.title: Bapineuzumab 302 (ApoE4 Carrier)
trial_pages.description: Phase 3 trial evaluating bapineuzumab in APOE4 carriers with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.sponsor: JANSSEN Alzheimer Immunotherapy Research & Development, LLC
trial_pages.population: Patients aged 50-88 with probable Alzheimer's disease, MMSE 16-26 (APOE4 carriers)
trial_pages.why_md: This trial tested whether clearing amyloid plaques with bapineuzumab could slow cognitive and functional decline in APOE4 carriers with established mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
status_log_md: **2014-01-23** — Primary results published in NEJM, showing no clinical benefit ([doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1304839](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1304839)).
trial_pages.results_md: Bapineuzumab failed to show significant differences compared to placebo on the primary clinical endpoints (ADAS-cog11 and DAD). While the drug successfully stabilized brain amyloid and reduced CSF phospho-tau, it caused dose-dependent amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA-E).

trial_pages.title: Bapineuzumab 301 (ApoE4 Non-Carrier)
trial_pages.description: Phase 3 trial evaluating bapineuzumab in APOE4 noncarriers with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.sponsor: JANSSEN Alzheimer Immunotherapy Research & Development, LLC
trial_pages.population: Patients aged 50-88 with probable Alzheimer's disease, MMSE 16-26 (APOE4 noncarriers)
trial_pages.why_md: This parallel Phase 3 trial evaluated bapineuzumab specifically in APOE4 noncarriers to determine if anti-amyloid therapy had different safety and efficacy profiles based on genetic risk factors.
status_log_md: **2014-01-23** — Primary results published in NEJM, noting a severe confounding factor with baseline amyloid negativity ([doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1304839](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1304839)).
trial_pages.results_md: The trial missed its primary clinical endpoints. Retrospective biomarker analysis revealed that over a third (36.1%) of enrolled noncarriers lacked amyloid pathology at baseline, severely confounding the results and invalidating much of the clinical data for this subgroup.

timeline_entries.title: 2012-08 — Intravenous bapineuzumab program terminated
timeline_entries.body_md: Pfizer and Janssen discontinue all global Phase 3 trials of the anti-amyloid antibody bapineuzumab after [North American trials](/research/papers/bapineuzumab-phase-3-mild-moderate) fail to show clinical benefit in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
